title: Saturn's rings — 270,000 km across, about 10 meters thick

segments.en: Saturn's rings are about ten meters thick,
segments.en_cap: Saturn's rings are | about 10 meters thick,

segments.en: yet two hundred seventy thousand kilometers across.
Between Earth and the Moon, they'd span seventy percent of the gap.

segments.en: Shrink them to paper thickness, and they'd still be almost three kilometers across.

segments.en: Up close, they split into ringlets and gaps, one kept open by a moon just twenty-eight kilometers wide.

segments.en: countless chunks of almost pure water ice, from specks of dust to blocks as big as a house.
segments.en_cap: countless chunks | of almost pure water ice, | from specks of dust | to blocks | as big as a house.

segments.en: Each circles Saturn at about sixty thousand kilometers an hour, yet neighbors drift by at a snail's pace: millimeters per second.

segments.en: Crush all that ice into one ball, and it would be about three hundred twenty kilometers wide: smaller than Saturn's little moon Mimas.

segments.en: And it's raining onto Saturn: an Olympic pool's worth every half hour.
